messages:
sarah-sales: Heads-up — POC for Jupiter (payments startup). Their rerank flow is failing: getting a dims mismatch error when comparing incoming embeddings to the stored index, and we also saw intermittent 429s during bulk-ingest. Can the swarm take a look?

kai-ml: paste the exact error and a sample request/response if you have it.

sarah-sales: here — from their app logs:
```
ERROR: ValueError: incoming vector size 1536 does not match index dimension 1024
HTTP 200 (embed) returned vector length=1536
/compare -> 400 {\"error\": \"dimension mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536\"}
```

infra-bot: ratelimit: 429 returned for /v1/embeddings bulk endpoint; headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 24

jon-eng: two likely causes: 1) model mismatch — client is requesting a newer embed model (1536d) while the index was built with older 1024d vectors, or 2) they accidentally used token embeddings vs text embeddings (rare). Also 429 suggests their ingest batching is too aggressive.

maria-se: what model name did they call? If they switched from embed-v1 -> embed-v2 we changed dims in v2. If so we need to re-index or pin the model during POC.

sarah-sales: they called model: "embed-sim-large" (that's their caller) — customer said they didn't change code. They are using our hosted API via our JS SDK.

kai-ml: ask them to paste the exact SDK param. Also request \"model\" from their /v1/embeddings call. Meanwhile quick mitigation: set the reranker to accept either model by adding a model-compat check or return a 400 instructing to re-index.

jon-eng: practical steps: 1) confirm the model name in the embedding response payload (we echo model in response). 2) if index dims != response dims then re-index OR re-run embeddings with the older model. 3) lower their batch size during POC (try 8-16) to avoid 429s.

amos-support: Regarding 429s and POC capacity: we can temporarily bump their quota for the POC window (48h) if sales provides the customer name + expected qps. Also we have a one-off reserved burst plan for POCs — <https://redwood.example.com/pricing/poc-burst>.

maria-se: here's a quick curl example to show model in response — ask them to run and paste results:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embed-sim-large","input":["sample text"]}' | jq .
```
Look for the top-level "model" and the "data[0].embedding | length"

sarah-sales: I ran that against their key and got: 
```json
{
  "model": "embed-sim-large",
  "data": [{"embedding": [/* 1536 floats */]}]
}
```
So it's definitely returning 1536. Their index was built earlier with "embed-base-1024".

jon-eng: ok that confirms. Two paths: A) re-index with 1536 vectors (recommended long-term), or B) serve a compatibility route: make their reranker call our legacy model name (embed-base-1024) by explicitly setting model param in their client. B is fastest for POC.

maria-se: for the 429s: check their batch_size and concurrency. If they're doing 128 items per request or >8 concurrent requests you'll hit our burst protections. Suggest payload: {"input": [...], "batch_size": 16} and add exponential backoff on 429s.

amos-support: I'll prepare a short POC quote for reserved capacity (48h uplift + 2x baseline qps). Sarah, can you send me the customer name and the target qps?

sarah-sales: sending offline. Quick Q from customer: will switching to embed-base-1024 reduce quality? They asked about retrieval/metrics impact and cost delta.

kai-ml: yes, embed-base will be slightly different quality vs large model. For reranking POC, differences are usually small for short retrievals, but their benchmarks will tell. Cost: large model is ~2.5x the token/embed cost. Recommend running a small 200-sample A/B to quantify.

jon-eng: also note: if they re-index we'll need to re-run their offline embedding job (we can help with a one-off bulk job via infra team). That avoids changing their serving code.

infra-bot: bulk-job-scheduler: Request queued (job-id: qb-1773001). Estimated completion 23m.

sarah-sales: action items: 1) ask customer to explicitly set model param to embed-base-1024 in their SDK if they want quick fix OR 2) approve re-index and temporary POC quota bump. 2) reduce batch/concurrency and add backoff for 429s. 3) run quick A/B on quality (200 samples).

maria-se: I can drop a short snippet for our SDK to pin model + safe batching.

maria-se: snippet:
```js
const client = new Redwood({ key: process.env.KEY });
const res = await client.embeddings.create({ model: 'embed-base-1024', input: texts, batch_size: 16 });
// on 429 -> retry with 500ms * 2^attempts
```

sarah-sales: customer accepted option B (pin model) for now and wants re-index later. They asked for a formal note on bandwidth bump — Amos please send the quote.

amos-support: Will do, sending quote + temporary quota lift now.

sarah-sales: confirmed: re-run after changes — no dims mismatch on our end now and fewer 429s. Scheduling a call tomorrow to confirm metrics. Thanks team :thumbsup:
